Do I need to install anything?
No. NetTango runs in your web browser. You do not need to install any software.
Do my students need to know how to code?
No. Students assemble blocks, and each model includes only the blocks its phenomenon requires. They do not need prior coding experience.
Nothing. NetTango is free and open source, developed at Northwestern's Center for Connected Learning by the NetLogo Foundation.

Designing lessons for a new topic?
Model real world phenomena from simple blocks

Each model provides blocks for a single phenomenon, such as ant foraging, gas particles, or spaceship flight. Students work only with the blocks that phenomenon requires, without first learning a programming language.

In Antomology Introduction, students start with two blocks: one that moves the ants and one that makes them wander. Each later model in the sequence adds a few blocks, such as picking up food or dropping a chemical trail.
The Antomology Pheromones model running: ants carry food from the flowers to the nest and leave a chemical trail
Explore how ants use pheromones to find their way. Your students build the rule for laying a chemical trail and observe whether the ants mark a path back to the nest.
The Spaceship Programming model running: a ship fires its engines one at a time to fly through an L-shaped corridor to a green target
Explore how a spaceship moves when its engines fire. Your students schedule each engine with blocks and observe that the ship keeps moving until an opposing engine fires.
The Two Particles in a Box model running: two particles move and collide in a small box
Explore how gas particles interact in a closed box. Your students build the collision rule and observe how collisions change the motion of the particles.
